problem: Existing VLN agents rely only on visual observations and instructions, so they fail to disambiguate visually similar objects with different attributes (e.g., rectangular vs. circular tables) because they lack common-sense knowledge. Prior knowledge-augmented methods (CKR, KERM, ACK) can also introduce noise or data bias from the external knowledge.
motivation: In complex scenes with many similar landmarks, instruction-to-environment matching is ambiguous, and common-sense descriptions could help. However, naively adding a large knowledge base injects bias (the KB noun distribution differs from that of the instructions, as the word clouds show), so knowledge must be filtered by what the instruction actually mentions.
key_idea: Retrieve descriptive knowledge from a 630K-sentence Visual Genome-based KB via CLIP matching of image sub-regions, then filter it using landmark noun phrases from the instruction (KGL) and fuse it dynamically with instruction and vision features (KGDA) on top of DUET.
insight: Knowledge helps only when it is landmark-guided and gated: the ablation on REVERIE val-unseen shows that adding KGL or KGDA alone raises SR/RGS but lowers SPL/RGSPL (e.g., SPL 33.73 to 32.05 with KGL only), whereas combining both gives the best results (SPL 34.38, RGSPL 24.42). The sigmoid dynamic gating gives a further gain on test-unseen (SR 57.10 to 57.68), consistent with the view that instructions should dominate and knowledge only assist.
method: Knowledge Base Construction: following KERM, converts Visual Genome attribute-object pairs and subject-verb-object triples into canonical forms, giving 630K language descriptions (KB1); a noun-only version (KB2, extracted with spaCy en_core_web_sm) is aligned one-to-one.

Knowledge Matching: splits each view into 5 sub-regions; CLIP-I encodes sub-regions as queries and CLIP-T encodes KB2 nouns as keys; the top-5 nouns by cosine similarity per sub-region are replaced by their full descriptions from KB1.

Knowledge Guided by Landmark (KGL): a cross-attention layer (knowledge as query, instruction noun phrases/landmarks as key and value), followed by self-attention and an FFN, yielding landmark-guided knowledge features.
Cross-modal knowledge-object fusion: an LXMERT-style local cross-modal encoder fuses object features with the knowledge features to give enhanced object features.

KGDA instruction augmentation: multi-head attention (instruction as query, knowledge as key/value) produces knowledge-enhanced instructions, which are mixed with the original instruction via a sigmoid gate, A = w*I'' + (1-w)*I; a similar dynamic adjustment is applied to the local features.
Dynamic fusion / action decision: DUET-style global (topological map) and local branches are combined with an FFN-computed sigmoid weight to give the action scores.
Training: initialized from pre-trained LXMERT, pre-trained with MRC, MLM, SAP (plus OG for REVERIE) and EnvEdit features, using CLIP-B/16 visual features.

setting.backbone: DUET-based dual-scale graph transformer with LXMERT-initialized cross-modal encoders and CLIP-B/16 features (trained/fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: R2R and REVERIE training data with MRC/MLM/SAP/OG pre-training plus EnvEdit augmentation; external KB of 630K descriptions from Visual Genome
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, CLIP-B/16 features) with 5 sub-regions per view, object bounding boxes (REVERIE), GPS position
setting.privileged: none (REVERIE uses provided object bounding boxes, as is standard)

results: LGK reaches R2R val-unseen SR 75 / SPL 65 / NE 2.69 and test-unseen SR 74 / SPL 64, beating BEVBert (SR 73, SPL 62 on test) and the DUET baseline (SR 69, SPL 59). On REVERIE test-unseen it gets SR 57.68, SPL 40.63 and RGS 35.28, ahead of VER (SR 56.82, SPL 38.76, RGS 33.88).
limitations: Gains over the strongest baselines are small (about 1 point on several metrics), and no variance or multiple runs are reported.

The KB comes from Visual Genome, so it contains data bias; the paper only mitigates it via landmarks and does not remove it. Retrieval quality and the 5-sub-region CLIP matching are not analysed in the ablations.
Evaluation is limited to discrete-environment R2R and REVERIE, with no continuous-environment or real-robot tests; the ablations are minimal and no KB-size or top-k study is given.
